items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: And he called desperately to find somebody. He called the hotel. They lived in the hotel where I was playing with this so-called orchestra.

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah there was a troupe on the road. I was playing with this rinky-dink band in Colorado at a hotel which is now torn down mercifully, in Denver. And it sounds like a cheap film plot, but they came through, Judy and Mickey were starting to do the Andy Hardy series at MGM, it was the late ‘30s. And MGM sent them out on what we call a “trip to huckster everything.” And Mickey would do half of his father’s act. His father was a burlesque comic, Joe Ewell. And Mickey would do the clean part of his father’s act,…

never happen but it does. And a gentleman by the name of Frank Perquette was the tour manager for MGM so-called. And he called desperately to find somebody. He called the hotel. They lived in the hotel where I was playing with this so-called orchestra. And I think he called the hotel manager or something and asked if I could be sent down to help them out. And the hotel manager was wonderful, he said that I read music. And I thought that that was the most wonderful recommendation. And a day later here I am on the…
And you gave a twelve hour notice to the rinky-dink orchestra.
